subject: jumping spider
title: Out of 40,000 Spider Species, Exactly One Is Mostly Vegetarian

scenes.text: Of 40,000 spider species, one is mostly vegetarian.
It's a jumping spider from Mexico and Central America, built like any other hunter.
But it lives on acacia trees and eats the rich nubs that grow on the leaf tips.
Those nubs are meant for ants, which guard the tree and attack anything that lands on it.
So the spider steals. It dodges patrols, leaps away when cornered, and drops on a silk line.
In Mexico, plants made up about 90 percent of its diet. A spider that robs ants for salad.

description:
Of roughly 40,000 known spider species, one eats mostly plants.
Bagheera kiplingi is a jumping spider of Mexico and Central America that lives on acacia trees. The trees grow nutritious leaf-tip nodules called Beltian bodies to feed the ants that defend them; the spider steals them, avoiding the ant patrols by nesting on old leaves, jumping away and dropping on silk lines. In Mexico plant food made up about 90 percent of its diet (91 percent in one count), and in Costa Rica about 60 percent; it sometimes takes nectar, ant larvae, flies and even its own kind. The behaviour was first seen by Eric Olson in Costa Rica in 2001 and by Christopher Meehan in Mexico in 2007, and published in Current Biology in 2009.
Would you still call it a predator? Comment below.
first_comment: It still eats the odd ant larva, and occasionally one of its own kind. Would you still call it a predator?
